title: Local killing of an equalizer cohomology class
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a category small in a universe containing the sites and coefficients [def-weil-size-convention], endowed with two site structures $\tau$ and $\tau'$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] such that every $\tau'$-covering is a $\tau$-covering. For $X\in\mathcal C$, let $\mathcal C_\tau/X$ and $\mathcal C_{\tau'}/X$ be the slice sites: their objects are arrows $U\to X$, their morphisms are commutative triangles, and their coverings are those whose underlying families cover $U$ in the respective topology. Let $\epsilon_X:\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C_\tau/X)\to\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C_{\tau'}/X)$ be the comparison geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism] with direct image the identity on underlying presheaves and inverse image $\tau$ sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. For $f:X\to Y$ write $f_{\tau'}$ for the relocalization morphism of slice topoi whose inverse image sends $H$ to $(U\to X)\mapsto H(U\to X\to Y)$. Higher direct images below mean the ordinary right derived functors on abelian sheaves, computed using injective resolutions. Suppose that a class $\mathcal P$ of morphisms and full subcategories $\mathcal A'_X\subset\mathrm{Ab}(\mathcal C_{\tau'}/X)$ have the following properties. Each $\mathcal A'_X$ contains zero and is closed under isomorphisms, kernels and cokernels of morphisms between its objects, and extensions (the weak Serre condition). Assume in addition:

(1) For $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathcal P$ and any $Y'\to Y$, the fibre product $X\times_Y Y'$ exists and $X\times_Y Y'\to Y'$ lies in $\mathcal P$.

(2) For every $f:X\to Y$, one has $f_{\tau'}^{-1}(\mathcal A'_Y)\subset\mathcal A'_X$.

(3) Every $H'\in\mathcal A'_X$ already satisfies the $\tau$ sheaf condition on $\mathcal C/X$.

(4) For $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathcal P$, $H'\in\mathcal A'_X$ and every $i\geq0$, one has $R^if_{\tau',*}H'\in\mathcal A'_Y$.

Let $f:X\to Y$ be in $\mathcal P$ and let $\{X\to Y\}$ be a singleton $\tau$-covering. Let $H'\in\mathcal A'_Y$ and $q\geq1$. Write $H'|_T$ for sectionwise restriction to the slice site over $T\to Y$. If
$$\theta\in H^q_{\tau'}(X,H'|_X),\qquad \operatorname{pr}_1^*\theta=\operatorname{pr}_2^*\theta\ \text{in }H^q_{\tau'}(X\times_YX,H'|_{X\times_YX}),$$
then there exists a $\tau'$-covering $\{Y_j\to Y\}$ such that $\theta$ pulls back to zero in $H^q_{\tau'}(Y_j\times_YX,H'|_{Y_j\times_YX})$ for every $j$.

source.place: Tag 0EZD, lemma-make-class-zero-general; naturality/canonical maps are those of its proof and section-compare-general.

proof.text: Work on $\mathcal D=\mathcal C_{\tau'}/Y$. By localization of object cohomology, identify $H^q_{\tau'}(T,H'|_T)$ with $H^q(T,H')$ for every $T\to Y$. These identifications are natural in arrows over $Y$. In particular all pullbacks below are restrictions of object cohomology on this single site: they can be computed by the restriction maps of one injective resolution of $H'$ on $\mathcal D$.

source.place: Tag 0EZD, lemma-make-class-zero-general, proof; the canonical cohomology-presheaf maps of Tag 072W, lemma-higher-direct-images.

proof.text: The base-change functor $u:\mathcal D\to\mathcal C_{\tau'}/X$ sends $(V\to Y)$ to $(V\times_YX\to X)$; its products exist by (1). It preserves coverings and their pullbacks, since these are the base-changed families in the site axioms. The direct image of the given relocalization is $(f_{\tau',*}K)(V)=K(V\times_YX\to X)$. Indeed the adjunction with restriction is explicit: from $a:F|_X\to K$ obtain $F(V)\to F(V\times_YX)\xrightarrow{a}K(V\times_YX)$; conversely evaluate a map $F\to u^sK$ at $(U\to Y)$ and then restrict $K(U\times_YX)\to K(U\to X)$ along the graph of $U\to X$. Naturality and the two projection-graph identities show these assignments are inverse. The same formulas on sheaves of sets give the adjunction to the specified inverse image of the relocalization. This inverse image preserves finite limits because the given relocalization is a geometric morphism. Thus this continuous $u$ presents that morphism of sites.

source.place: Tag 0EZD, lemma-make-class-zero-general, proof; the canonical cohomology-presheaf maps of Tag 072W, lemma-higher-direct-images.

proof.text: Put $\mathcal G'=R^qf_{\tau',*}(H'|_X)$ and $P(V)=H^q(V\times_YX\to X,H'|_X)$. The higher-direct-image theorem identifies $\mathcal G'$ canonically with the $\tau'$-sheafification of $P$. Using Step 1, regard $P(V)$ as $H^q(V\times_YX,H')$. Write $e_V:P(V)\to\mathcal G'(V)$ for the canonical map. Its restriction along $a:V'\to V$ is induced by $a\times_Y\mathrm{id}_X$, and $e$ is a natural morphism of presheaves. Set $\overline\theta=e_Y(\theta)$, using $Y\times_YX\cong X$.

source.place: Tag 0EZD, lemma-make-class-zero-general, proof; the canonical cohomology-presheaf maps of Tag 072W, lemma-higher-direct-images.

proof.text: Apply the same higher-direct-image theorem to the identity morphism of $\mathcal D$: the presheaf $Q(V)=H^q(V,H')$ has sheafification $R^q\mathrm{id}_*H'=0$. The last equality follows by applying the identity to an injective resolution, whose positive cohomology sheaves vanish by its definition and $q>0$. Abelian sheafification is sheafification on underlying sets, so local equality for sheafification applied to $\theta,0\in Q(X)$ gives a $\tau'$-covering $\{W_k\to X\}$ with $\theta|_{W_k}=0$ for every $k$. This derives the locality input directly from the cited statements.

source.place: Tag 0EZD, lemma-make-class-zero-general, proof; the canonical cohomology-presheaf maps of Tag 072W, lemma-higher-direct-images.

proof.text: Write $X\times_YX$ with $\operatorname{pr}_1$ the projection to the base object $X\to Y$ in $P(X)$ and $\operatorname{pr}_2$ the projection to the coefficient slice $\mathcal C/X$. Naturality of $e$ gives $\overline\theta|_X=e_X(\operatorname{pr}_2^*\theta)$. The equalizer hypothesis therefore gives $\overline\theta|_X=e_X(\operatorname{pr}_1^*\theta)$. For $a_k:W_k\to X$, the restriction of $\operatorname{pr}_1^*\theta\in P(X)$ to $P(W_k)$ is the pullback of $\theta|_{W_k}$ along $W_k\times_YX\to W_k$, hence zero. This equality is simply the composition identity $\operatorname{pr}_1\circ(a_k\times\mathrm{id}_X)=a_k\circ\operatorname{pr}_{W_k}$ on the common section complex of Step 1.

source.place: Tag 0EZD, lemma-make-class-zero-general, proof; the canonical cohomology-presheaf maps of Tag 072W, lemma-higher-direct-images.

proof.text: The $\tau'$-sheaf $\mathcal G'$ is separated for $\{W_k\to X\}$. The image $e_X(\operatorname{pr}_1^*\theta)$ restricts to zero on every $W_k$ by Step 5, so it is zero. Thus $\overline\theta|_X=0$.

source.place: Tag 0EZD, lemma-make-class-zero-general, proof; the canonical cohomology-presheaf maps of Tag 072W, lemma-higher-direct-images.

proof.text: Assumption (2) puts $H'|_X$ in $\mathcal A'_X$. Since $f\in\mathcal P$, assumption (4) puts $\mathcal G'$ in $\mathcal A'_Y$, and (3) makes $\mathcal G'$ a $\tau$-sheaf. The singleton $\tau$-covering $\{X\to Y\}$ therefore makes $\mathcal G'(Y)\to\mathcal G'(X)$ injective by the sheaf equalizer condition. As $\overline\theta|_X=0$, it follows that $\overline\theta=0$.

source.place: Tag 0EZD, lemma-make-class-zero-general, proof; the canonical cohomology-presheaf maps of Tag 072W, lemma-higher-direct-images.

proof.text: Now $e_Y(\theta)=e_Y(0)$ in $P^\#(Y)=\mathcal G'(Y)$. Apply the underlying-set compatibility and local equality theorem for sheafification to $P$: there is a $\tau'$-covering $\{Y_j\to Y\}$ such that $\theta|_{Y_j}=0$ in $P(Y_j)$. By the definition of $P$ and the natural localization isomorphism, these are exactly the required zero classes in $H^q_{\tau'}(Y_j\times_YX,H'|_{Y_j\times_YX})$.
